title: SeqFusion: slot-concatenation dynamic packing to minimize padding amplification
author: Marina Velasquez
release_notes: Introduce SeqFusion slot-concatenation packing: reduces average padding tokens by ~28% for mixed-length workloads. Backwards-compatible; runtime auto-enables under heuristics. Improvements to KV cache routing and kernel alignment.
description:
Motivation: production inference traces show significant pad amplification when many short requests (seqlen <= 16) occupy their own slots. Traditional bucketing reduces that but still leaves sub-slot wasted token capacity and causes extra KV cache entries and kernel launch overhead. This change implements SeqFusion: a slot-concatenation packing heuristic that coalesces multiple short sequences into a single execution slot while preserving per-request KV isolation and stream-level latency SLOs.

Design summary: SeqFusion creates 'micro-cohorts' of short requests that are concatenated into a single padded buffer up to a per-slot soft-capacity (configurable, defaults to 512 tokens). The runtime treats the fused slot as a single sequence for kernel execution but maintains a mapping table to demultiplex outputs back to original requests. To keep latency bounded we: (1) enforce a jitter-aware hold window (default 12ms) before fusion, (2) prioritize unfused long sequences to avoid head-of-line blocking, and (3) fall back to standard bucketing for edge cases (very high entropy length distributions). Key implementation points: kernel alignment pads the fused sequence to nearest vector-width boundary to retain efficient GEMM paths; KV cache entries are stored per-original-request but preallocated in a contiguous memory slab for the fused slot to improve cacheline locality; the scheduler updates slot accounting to include fused-count heuristics so autoscaler sees realistic effective throughput.

Review conversation (selected):
- Jared Lin (review): "I like the approach — two concerns: 1) the hold-window might increase P99 for short requests under heavy load, and 2) memory accounting for fused slabs needs to be hedged against OOM bursts. Can you add a safety valve to disable fusion when mem pressure is high?"
- Marina (author): "Added auto-disable when overall slab usage > 78% and a per-node backpressure metric exposing 'fusion_disabled_by_mem'. Also tightened hold-window to be jitter-aware (exp backoff) to limit p99 regressions; added tests."
- Priya Raman (review): "Verified on perf harness: mixed-length trace (80% seqlen<=16) shows token/sec +19% and pad tokens -28% with tail latency within SLOs. Please add an observability note to the ops doc."
- Owen Castillo (approve): "Looks good; small nit on naming (fused_count -> fused_slot_count) addressed in follow-up commit."

CI summary: initial run failed lint on naming conventions; fixed. GPU perf suite (r18) shows +12% throughput overall and better kernel occupancy on short-seq workloads. Regression tests for KV eviction pass. All green on second run.

Safety and rollback: SeqFusion is feature-flagged (runtime config: "seqfusion.enabled") and defaulted ON for mixed-length queue profiles only. Added runtime metric "fusion_disabled_by_mem" and an operator-facing runtime toggle in the console; rollback route: set seqfusion.enabled=false and drain node, revert head_branch if incidents persist.

Merge: squash and merge; changelog entry added under runtime/perf. Merge method: squash/merge.

notes: This change is complementary to existing bucketing strategies: SeqFusion targets many small concurrent requests without increasing inter-request padding. It intentionally keeps KV entries per-request to simplify security/audit boundaries while co-locating memory to improve locality.
operational_guidance: Enable seqfusion for queues with median seqlen <= 24. If fusion_disabled_by_mem > 0.05 for >5m, investigate slab fragmentation and consider raising slab-capacity or disabling fusion on the node. Observe fused_slot_count and pad_amplification metrics after enabling.
risk_mitigation: Feature-flagged, memory auto-disable, hold-window adaptivity, fallback to existing bucketing, additional e2e tests added.
performance_summary: Mixed-length perf harness (trace: 120k requests; 80% seqlen<=16, 20% seqlen>128): avg throughput +19% token/sec, pad-token reduction -28%, p95 latency change +1.8ms (within SLO), p99 unchanged. Kernel occupancy improved on short sequences (measured via occupancy sampler).
